title: Add sparse four-endpoint observability census
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This is an exact observability census on both pinned orientations of the PR2979 word, extended from pairs and triples to all `49 choose 4 = 211,876` four-class supports of rank-seven endpoints. A complete GF(3) screen finds 1,353 candidate supports; each is rechecked over the rationals. Every candidate has a rank-nine join and exposes eligible forms.

The quartet census adds six exact scalar readout identities beyond the triple census: four use five input coordinates, one uses eight and one uses ten. Together they span the same five-dimensional block; the four five-coordinate forms span dimension three. Their readouts use nine distinct terminal registers across seven rank-seven endpoint classes. The rank-nine join is not a free common helper.

These are linear-information identities, not a supplier or caller-facing construction. No downstream consumer, physical realization, complete recursive invoice or κ improvement is claimed. The selected κ remains `0.001672660197076918`.

## Task and overlap

Task card `complex-new-helper-inventory`, priority revision 6; scope changed to test whether pooling incomparable endpoint observations yields a sparse basis, as recorded in `research/cross-endframe-observability/TASK.json`. Base commit: `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`; the two word inputs are hash-pinned in `SOURCES.json`.

The closest boundary is [PR #3172](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3172), whose fixed-endpoint obstruction explicitly leaves pooling incomparable endpoints outside its scope. This package tests that boundary on the changed PR2979 word and does not claim the pooling idea as new or generalize beyond the two pinned orientations. The cached overlap scan covers 394 open PRs and 2,319 discussions as of 2026-10-18 03:15 UTC, but refresh failed; it is not a novelty certificate.

## Validation

The checker uses the Python standard library; replayed with Python 3.12:

```sh
python3 -B research/cross-endframe-observability/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/cross-endframe-observability --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/cross-endframe-observability
```

It reconstructs both pinned word orientations and exact formal-warp adjoints; checks all endpoint singletons, 1,176 pairs, 18,424 triples and 211,876 four-class supports; screens quartets over GF(3); and rechecks all 1,353 candidates over `Q`. The two orientations agree. Protected columns and nonempty warp words cancel, and register-deletion controls challenge the rank-eight witness. The finite census does not prove a caller, physical implementation or full recursive invoice.

## Credit

The word providers and predecessor attribution from PR #2979 are retained. Ross Richardson's [PR #3172](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3172) supplies the stated pooling boundary. Prepared by OpenAI Codex with substantial AI assistance; no independent human review or formal-kernel review is claimed. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

1. Does an actual downstream call consume the sparse six-form block or its five-dimensional span? Trace the forms to a named producer/consumer boundary and compare the required subspace with their span; the four five-term forms alone span only three dimensions. No matching caller is identified.
2. Can the seven-endpoint, nine-register observation be implemented and priced below the rank-nine transfer allowance? For a matched caller, derive the multi-register circuit, chronology, dirty-state restoration, storage and recursive profile. No complete physical or recursive invoice exists; stop if the caller does not consume the block or the full budget misses its target.
